titleStmt.title: Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons: Bibliographical Authority

publicationStmt.p: Working authority file for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: The initial bibliographical records. Missing publication details are identified explicitly for later completion.

projectDesc.p: This file identifies published editions, manuscript catalogues, scholarly studies, and digital reference resources cited across the corpus. It is distinct from works.xml, which identifies textual works, and from manuscript, colophon, and witness authority records.

editorialDecl.p: Bibliographical identifiers follow the pattern bibl-000001. Allocate each identifier once and retain it when citation metadata is corrected. Distinguish editions, volumes, translations, and other publication versions when necessary to identify the item actually cited.

Use one record per cited bibliographical item inside listBibl. Prefer biblStruct for books, journal articles, and chapters with structured metadata. Use bibl for digital resources or other sources better represented by a flexible citation.

For articles and chapters, analytic describes the cited contribution and monogr its journal or containing volume. Title levels are a for contributions, m for books, and j for journals. Preserve original titles and author names; add transliterated or translated title forms only when useful and explicitly distinguish them using title/@type and appropriate language tags.

Record contributors in publication order, repeating author or editor as necessary. Names of modern scholars may remain directly in the citation; a persons.xml authority entry is not required solely because someone is an author or editor. Link a name to an existing person record when useful and securely identified. Other responsibilities can use respStmt where needed.
Record publication place, publisher, and date in imprint.
Use idno in the relevant monogr or analytic for verified identifiers such as DOI, ISBN, or ISSN.

References from other authority files use bibliography.xml#bibl-000001. Edition files use a relative path appropriate to their location. Citation display and punctuation will be generated from this structured data according to the project's agreed style; no particular display style is fixed here.
